<!--
===============================================================================
WHAT THIS DOCUMENT DOES  (read this before running)
===============================================================================
This is the DEMAND-SIDE script of the CBA -> employment pipeline. It turns the
cost-benefit (CBA) output into signed GLORIA-product demand vectors, then
multiplies them by the pre-computed employment matrix L to get domestic jobs.

It replaces the old "$1M-per-strategy" scaffold
("Sisepuede - Transformation demand vectors for GLORIA.Rmd"). Three upgrades:

  1. VALUES ARE CBA DOLLARS, NOT $1M. Each transformation's demand is
     multiplier x delta(physical quantity between scenario and BAU runs),
     split into a COST stream (+) and a SAVINGS stream (-). See Section 4.
  2. JOBS COME FROM THE L MATRIX, NOT FROM RE-RUNNING MINDSET. We built L once
     in Python (EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py). Here we just do jobs = L %*% f in R.
     L already encodes the Leontief inverse, 2019 employment coefficients, and
     the import-origin split; it returns DOMESTIC jobs only. See Section 6.
  3. ELECTRICITY MIX IS DYNAMIC & SCENARIO-BASED (per-year), not the static
     2019 IEA mix used in the old code. See Section 3. (Optional; see flags.)

DESIGN CHOICE (agreed): the cost structure is treated as a BILL OF MATERIALS in
FINAL-DEMAND space -- "$x is spent buying product g" -- and L was built to match
that. We do NOT route it through MINDSET's capital-formation converter (that
step is for "who invests" vectors and would double-process a bill of materials).

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PIPELINE MAP (which section produces what)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  S1  Setup + paths ....................... libraries, file locations
  S2  Cost structures (Eora26 x strategy) .. the sector weights per transformation
  S3  Dynamic electricity mix [OPTIONAL] ... per-year grid composition (scenario)
  S4  CBA dollar scaling .................... multiplier x delta -> signed $ per strategy
  S5  Eora26 -> GLORIA (120 products) ....... spread each sector weight to products
  S6  Employment ........................... jobs = L %*% f  (domestic)
  S7  Export + diagnostics

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FILES STILL NEEDED FROM FERNANDO  (script runs without them; sections skip)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [PENDING-1] COST-STRUCTURE MASTER. Two candidates exist on disk:
        (a) Data/.../ATTRIBUTE_STRATEGY_transformations_vectors.xlsx  (spine-native, OLD)
        (b) Data/Cost Structure/Transformations - Cost Structure vectors (SSP CBA).xlsx (NEW, 18 sheets)
      Set COST_MASTER below to whichever is authoritative. Default = (a).
  [PENDING-2] STRATEGY RE-KEY CROSSWALK: Fernando's finished
        old strategy_id  <->  new strategy_code / output_variable_name  map.
      Set REKEY_FILE + its key columns in S4 when ready. Until then, S4 joins
      the CBA lines to strategies on the subsector token as a STOPGAP and flags it.

Everything else needed already exists (paths verified 2026-07-25):
  - L matrix .................. MINDSET_module-main/SSP - Results/L_matrix_MAR.csv
  - GLORIA-Eora26 crosswalk ... Data/Crosswalks/GLORIA-Eora26 - Crosswalk.xlsx
  - GLORIA product numbers .... Data/SSP - Supporting Files/Gloria - Product list number.xlsx
  - CBA transformation costs .. Data/Edmundo/transformation_cost.csv
  - Physical quantities ....... Data/CBA/.../decomposed_ssp_output.csv  (wide; read with care)

```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

# S1. Setup and file locations

All paths are RELATIVE to the repo root, so the script is portable across
machines that have the three repos synced. Edit only this block if files move.

```{r paths}
# ---- Repo root -------------------------------------------------------------
# Set once. Everything else hangs off this. Adjust if your working dir differs.
REPO <- "Repos/SSP-employment_estimates"
MINDSET <- file.path(REPO, "MINDSET_module-main")

# ---- Scope (v1 = Morocco only; loop-ready) ---------------------------------
COUNTRY_ISO     <- "MAR"
COUNTRY_NAME    <- "Morocco"
COUNTRY_NAME_LC <- "morocco"   # region label as it appears in decomposed_ssp_output.csv

# ---- Inputs that EXIST (verified) ------------------------------------------
L_MATRIX_FILE   <- file.path(MINDSET, "SSP - Results", paste0("L_matrix_", COUNTRY_ISO, ".csv"))
CROSSWALK_FILE  <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Crosswalks/GLORIA-Eora26 - Crosswalk.xlsx")
PRODUCT_NUM_FILE<- file.path(REPO, "Data/SSP - Supporting Files/Gloria - Product list number.xlsx")
# AUTHORITATIVE CBA source = transformation_costs tab of cb_config_params.xlsx
# (in the ssp_morocco repo). Edmundo/transformation_cost.csv is a STALE export
# missing clinker/manure(x3)/biogas/gas_recovery; the rekey was built on this xlsx.
SSP_MOROCCO   <- "Repos/ssp_morocco"
CBA_COST_FILE <- file.path(SSP_MOROCCO,
                  "ssp_modeling/cost-benefits/cb_config_files/cb_config_params.xlsx")
CBA_COST_SHEET <- "transformation_costs"
DECOMP_FILE     <- file.path(REPO, "Data/CBA/sisepuede_results/sisepuede_results_sisepuede_run_2026-07-16/decomposed_ssp_output.csv")

# ---- COST_MASTER: authoritative = NEW SSP CBA file (PENDING-1 RESOLVED) -----
# Some strategy columns here sum to <1 or 0 BY DESIGN: they are completed by the
# per-year electricity mix (S3) or by a source column, via the S2 supplement step.
COST_MASTER <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Cost Structure",
                         "Transformations - Cost Structure vectors (SSP CBA).xlsx")

# ---- REKEY crosswalk: CBA output_variable_name -> strategy_id (PENDING-2 RESOLVED)
# Built by Fernando; joins the authoritative cb_config_params.xlsx with zero misses.
REKEY_FILE <- file.path(REPO, "Data/Crosswalks/CBA_to_transformation_crosswalk_claude.csv")
REKEY_OVN_COL <- "output_variable_name"   # key on the CBA side
REKEY_ID_COL  <- "strategy_id_new"        # -> matches cost_struct$strategy_id

# ---- CBA run ids (from Session 7) ------------------------------------------
RUN_BAU      <- "72072"   # baseline
RUN_SCENARIO <- "73073"   # policy scenario

# ---- Output ----------------------------------------------------------------
OUT_DIR <- file.path(MINDSET, "GLORIA_template/Scenarios")
if (!dir.exists(OUT_DIR)) dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- Small helper: does a file exist? (used to skip pending sections) ------
have <- function(p) !is.na(p) && file.exists(p)

cat("File availability:\n")
for (f in c(L_MATRIX_FILE, CROSSWALK_FILE, PRODUCT_NUM_FILE, CBA_COST_FILE,
            DECOMP_FILE, COST_MASTER)) {
  cat(sprintf("  [%s] %s\n", ifelse(have(f), "OK  ", "MISS"), f))
}
cat(sprintf("  [%s] REKEY_FILE (PENDING-2)\n", ifelse(have(REKEY_FILE), "OK  ", "MISS")))
```

# S2. Cost structures (Eora26 sector x strategy)

**What this is.** For each transformation (strategy), a vector of weights over
Eora26 sectors that sums to 1: "of each dollar this transformation spends, what
fraction is bought from each sector." This is the object [PENDING-1] provides.

We read it into a tidy long table `cost_struct`:
`strategy_id | Sector (Eora26) | weight`, weights summing to 1 per strategy.

> IMPORTANT — DO NOT RENORMALIZE HERE. Some strategy columns in the master sum
> to <1 or exactly 0 BY DESIGN: they are completed by the per-year electricity
> mix (S3) or by a source column (e.g. Grid Upgrades, Industrial EE) in the S2b
> supplement step. Renormalizing now would erase the gap the supplement fills.
> Final renormalization happens ONCE, at the end of S2b, after supplementing.
>
> We therefore produce two objects here:
>   master_long   : the FULL long master (every column, incl. source columns like
>                   "Grid Upgrades") — needed by the S2b replace-with-source rule.
>   cost_struct0  : the raw numeric-id strategy columns only (may sum != 1).

```{r cost-structures}
if (have(COST_MASTER)) {
  sheets <- excel_sheets(COST_MASTER)
  read_one <- function(sh) { df <- read_excel(COST_MASTER, sheet = sh); df$.__sheet <- sh; df }
  raw_list <- lapply(sheets, read_one)

  # Each sheet: first column is the Eora26 Sector, the rest are value columns
  # (numeric strategy ids AND named source columns like "Coal", "Grid Upgrades").
  to_long <- function(df) {
    sector_col <- names(df)[1]
    df %>%
      rename(Sector = all_of(sector_col)) %>%
      select(-any_of(".__sheet")) %>%
      mutate(across(-Sector, as.numeric)) %>%
      pivot_longer(-Sector, names_to = "col", values_to = "weight") %>%
      mutate(weight = ifelse(is.na(weight), 0, weight))
  }
  master_long <- bind_rows(lapply(raw_list, to_long)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Sector)) %>%
    group_by(col, Sector) %>%                 # a column may appear on >1 sheet
    summarise(weight = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")

  # raw strategy structures = numeric-id columns only, NOT renormalized
  cost_struct0 <- master_long %>%
    filter(grepl("^[0-9]+$", col)) %>%
    rename(strategy_id = col)

  s0 <- cost_struct0 %>% group_by(strategy_id) %>% summarise(s = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("cost_struct0 (raw): %d strategies; %d sum to <0.999 (to be supplemented in S2b)\n",
              nrow(s0), sum(s0$s < 0.999)))
} else {
  master_long <- NULL; cost_struct0 <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S2] COST_MASTER not found. Set COST_MASTER in S1.\n")
}
```

# S3. Dynamic electricity mix  [OPTIONAL — needs one wide CSV]

**Why.** When a transformation demands (or saves) *electricity*, the sectors it
hits depend on the grid mix. The old code froze this at the 2019 IEA mix. We
replace it with the SCENARIO's actual per-year generation by technology, so the
electricity portion of a cost structure tracks the decarbonising grid.

**Source.** `nemomod_entc_annual_production_by_technology_pp_*` columns inside
the wide `decomposed_ssp_output.csv` (run `RUN_SCENARIO`, region = Morocco).
That file has ~4,100 columns; base-R read segfaults on this machine
(see checkpoint). We therefore read only the columns we need, via a name filter.

> STATUS: this section is structured but LEFT INERT by default (`RUN_S3 <- FALSE`)
> because it feeds an enhancement, not the core jobs number. Turn it on once you
> and Fernando confirm the exact technology-column names and the source->Eora26
> generation-sector map (Session 7 rename map). The core pipeline (S4-S6) runs
> without it; electricity then falls back to whatever the cost structure carries.

This step RUNS BY DEFAULT now (`RUN_S3 <- TRUE`): the supplement in S2 needs it.
It builds `elec_by_year`: for each `time_period`, a vector of Eora26-sector
weights (summing to 1) = the year's generation mix applied to the per-source
cost structures on the `Synthetic_ind_energy` tab of COST_MASTER.

```{r dynamic-electricity}
RUN_S3 <- TRUE

# scenario technology token -> Synthetic_ind_energy source column (verified map)
tech2src <- c(coal="Coal", coal_ccs="Coal", gas="Oil and Gas", gas_ccs="Oil and Gas",
              oil="Oil and Gas", hydropower="Hydro", solar="Solar", wind="Wind",
              geothermal="Geothermal", nuclear="Nuclear", biomass="Bioenergy",
              biogas="Bioenergy")   # ocean, waste_incineration -> no target (dropped)

elec_by_year <- NULL   # filled below; consumed by S2
elec_avg     <- NULL   # year-averaged fallback (used if a period is missing)

if (RUN_S3 && have(DECOMP_FILE) && have(COST_MASTER)) {
  # --- per-source cost structures from the master's Synthetic_ind_energy tab ---
  sie <- read_excel(COST_MASTER, sheet = "Synthetic_ind_energy")
  names(sie)[1] <- "Sector"
  src_struct <- sie %>%
    pivot_longer(-Sector, names_to = "source", values_to = "w") %>%
    mutate(w = ifelse(is.na(w), 0, w)) %>%
    filter(source %in% unname(tech2src))     # keep generation sources only

  # --- per-year generation shares from the scenario run (73073) ----------------
  hdr <- names(read.csv(DECOMP_FILE, nrows = 0, check.names = FALSE))
  tech_cols <- grep("nemomod_entc_annual_production_by_technology_pp", hdr, value = TRUE)
  id_cols   <- intersect(c("primary_id", "region", "time_period"), hdr)
  gen <- read.csv(DECOMP_FILE, check.names = FALSE)[, c(id_cols, tech_cols)]
  gen <- gen[gen$region == COUNTRY_NAME_LC & gen$primary_id == as.integer(RUN_SCENARIO), ]

  # long: period x tech share -> map to source -> renormalize (after dropping unmatched)
  gen_by_src <- gen %>%
    select(time_period, all_of(tech_cols)) %>%
    pivot_longer(-time_period, names_to = "tech", values_to = "gen") %>%
    mutate(tech = sub(".*_pp_", "", tech)) %>%
    filter(tech %in% names(tech2src)) %>%
    mutate(source = tech2src[tech]) %>%
    group_by(time_period, source) %>% summarise(gen = sum(gen), .groups = "drop")

  # share = source generation / TOTAL generation THAT YEAR. Denominator computed
  # via an explicit per-year join (group_by %>% mutate proved unreliable here and
  # divided by the grand total across all years instead of the year's total).
  yr_total <- gen_by_src %>% group_by(time_period) %>%
    summarise(gen_tot = sum(gen), .groups = "drop")
  shares <- gen_by_src %>% left_join(yr_total, by = "time_period") %>%
    mutate(share = ifelse(gen_tot > 0, gen / gen_tot, 0)) %>%
    select(time_period, source, share)

  # per-year Eora26 electricity vector = sum_source share * source_struct
  elec_by_year <- shares %>%
    inner_join(src_struct, by = "source", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    group_by(time_period, Sector) %>%
    summarise(elec_w = sum(share * w), .groups = "drop")

  # year-averaged fallback (single vector) — mirrors the old static BAU_Electricity slot
  elec_avg <- elec_by_year %>% group_by(Sector) %>%
    summarise(elec_w = mean(elec_w), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(elec_w = elec_w / sum(elec_w))

  yr_sums <- elec_by_year %>% group_by(time_period) %>% summarise(s = sum(elec_w), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("[S3] elec_by_year: %d periods; per-year sum range [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              nrow(yr_sums), min(yr_sums$s), max(yr_sums$s)))
} else {
  cat("[SKIP S3] needs DECOMP_FILE + COST_MASTER. Electricity supplement in S2 will be skipped.\n")
}
```

# S2b. Supplement + finalize cost structures (per year)

**Why this step exists.** Several strategy columns in the master are intentionally
incomplete; they are completed here per Fernando's supplement spec:

  - ELEC-ADD (`base + coef * Electricity`):
      3000 +0.12, 3010 +0.50, 3012 +0.10, 3018 +0.10, 3019 +0.44, 4000 +0.29
  - REPLACE with the whole electricity vector: 3013
  - REPLACE with a named source column: 3002 = "Grid Upgrades", 3008 = "Industrial EE"

Electricity is the **per-year** scenario mix from S3, so a supplemented strategy's
structure changes year to year (the grid decarbonises). Strategies not in the
spec pass through unchanged. Every strategy is renormalized to sum 1 at the end.
Output `cost_struct` carries a `time_period` column; non-supplemented strategies
are constant across periods (kept per-year for a uniform downstream join).

```{r cost-structures-finalize}
if (!is.null(cost_struct0)) {

  # --- supplement spec (from Fernando's code line; 0.44** read as 0.44*) -------
  elec_add    <- c("3000"=0.12, "3010"=0.50, "3012"=0.10, "3018"=0.10, "3019"=0.44, "4000"=0.29)
  replace_elec<- c("3013")
  replace_src <- c("3002"="Grid Upgrades", "3008"="Industrial EE")

  have_elec <- !is.null(elec_by_year)
  if (!have_elec)
    cat("[WARN S2b] No electricity vectors from S3; ELEC-ADD/REPLACE-ELEC strategies will be under-filled.\n")

  # periods to expand over (from S3; fallback to a single NA period if S3 inert)
  periods <- if (have_elec) sort(unique(elec_by_year$time_period)) else NA_integer_

  all_ids <- sort(unique(cost_struct0$strategy_id))

  # helper: electricity vector for a given period (per-year, else year-avg fallback)
  elec_vec <- function(tp) {
    if (!have_elec) return(tibble(Sector = character(), elec_w = numeric()))
    v <- elec_by_year %>% filter(time_period == tp)
    if (nrow(v) == 0) v <- elec_avg %>% mutate(time_period = tp)
    v %>% select(Sector, elec_w)
  }

  build_one <- function(id, tp) {
    base <- cost_struct0 %>% filter(strategy_id == id) %>% select(Sector, weight)
    if (id %in% names(elec_add)) {
      ev <- elec_vec(tp)
      out <- full_join(base, ev, by = "Sector") %>%
        mutate(weight = ifelse(is.na(weight), 0, weight),
               elec_w = ifelse(is.na(elec_w), 0, elec_w),
               w = weight + elec_add[[id]] * elec_w) %>% select(Sector, w)
    } else if (id %in% replace_elec) {
      out <- elec_vec(tp) %>% transmute(Sector, w = elec_w)
    } else if (id %in% names(replace_src)) {
      # source column lives in the FULL master (may be a non-generation column)
      out <- master_long %>% filter(col == replace_src[[id]]) %>%
        group_by(Sector) %>% summarise(w = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
    } else {
      out <- base %>% rename(w = weight)      # pass-through, unchanged
    }
    out %>% mutate(strategy_id = id, time_period = tp)
  }

  grid <- expand.grid(strategy_id = all_ids, time_period = periods,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cost_struct <- bind_rows(Map(build_one, grid$strategy_id, grid$time_period)) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    mutate(s = sum(w), weight = ifelse(s > 0, w / s, 0)) %>%   # renormalize ONCE, here
    ungroup() %>% select(strategy_id, time_period, Sector, weight)

  chk <- cost_struct %>% group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    summarise(s = sum(weight), .groups = "drop")
  nzero <- chk %>% filter(s < 1e-9) %>% distinct(strategy_id) %>% nrow()
  cat(sprintf("cost_struct (final): %d strategies x %d periods; sum!=1 (excl zero): %d; zero-structure: %d\n",
              n_distinct(cost_struct$strategy_id), length(periods),
              sum(chk$s > 1e-9 & abs(chk$s - 1) > 1e-6), nzero))
} else {
  cost_struct <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S2b] cost_struct0 missing (S2 did not run).\n")
}
```

# S4. CBA dollar scaling (signed cost and savings streams)

**The rule (Session 7).** Each CBA line is
`$ = multiplier x [ var(RUN_SCENARIO) - var(RUN_BAU) ]` per year — the multiplier
applies to the **delta** of the difference_variable, not its level. Two streams:

  - `technical_cost`   -> POSITIVE demand (spending)
  - `technical_savings`-> NEGATIVE demand (already stored negative in the file)

They are kept SEPARATE (different cost structures), then summed downstream:
net = cost + savings. We report gross(+), gross(-), and net side by side.
Savings are one-sided (no re-spending modeled) -> net jobs are a LOWER BOUND.

```{r cba-scaling}
if (have(CBA_COST_FILE)) {
  cba <- read_excel(CBA_COST_FILE, sheet = CBA_COST_SHEET) %>% as.data.frame()
  # Keep only included lines if an `include` flag is present.
  if ("include" %in% names(cba)) cba <- cba %>% filter(include %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE", 1))

  # Classify each line by its output_variable_name token (Session 3 rule).
  cba <- cba %>%
    mutate(
      flow = case_when(
        str_detect(output_variable_name, "technical_cost")    ~ "cost",
        str_detect(output_variable_name, "technical_savings") ~ "savings",
        TRUE                                                   ~ "other"
      ),
      # subsector token = 2nd token of output_variable_name (e.g. cb:inen:... -> inen)
      subsector = str_split_fixed(output_variable_name, ":", 3)[, 2]
    )

  cat("CBA lines by flow type:\n"); print(table(cba$flow))

  # --- Physical delta: multiplier x (scenario - BAU) --------------------------
  # PENDING DATA STEP: the per-year physical quantity of `difference_variable`
  # for RUN_SCENARIO and RUN_BAU lives in decomposed_ssp_output.csv. Wiring that
  # join needs the physical-variable -> column map confirmed with Fernando
  # (the INEN worked example). Until then we expose the formula and leave `delta`
  # as NA so nothing downstream silently uses a wrong number.
  cba <- cba %>% mutate(delta = NA_real_,             # <- fill from decomposed run
                        cba_dollars = multiplier * delta)  # signed $ (savings multiplier<0)

  cat("\n[NOTE S4] `delta` is NA pending the physical-quantity join",
      "(decomposed_ssp_output.csv). Formula is in place; fill `delta` to activate.\n")
} else {
  cba <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S4] CBA cost file not found.\n")
}
```

```{r rekey}
# Re-key CBA output_variable_name -> strategy_id used by cost_struct (PENDING-2 done).
if (!is.null(cba) && have(REKEY_FILE)) {
  rekey <- read.csv(REKEY_FILE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    select(all_of(c(REKEY_OVN_COL, REKEY_ID_COL))) %>%
    rename(output_variable_name = all_of(REKEY_OVN_COL),
           strategy_id = all_of(REKEY_ID_COL)) %>%
    mutate(strategy_id = ifelse(is.na(strategy_id) | strategy_id == "", NA,
                                as.character(as.integer(strategy_id))))
  cba <- cba %>% left_join(rekey, by = "output_variable_name")

  matched <- cba %>% filter(!is.na(strategy_id)) %>% nrow()
  unmatched <- cba %>% filter(is.na(strategy_id)) %>% pull(output_variable_name)
  cat(sprintf("[S4 rekey] %d/%d CBA lines carry a strategy_id.\n", matched, nrow(cba)))
  # Blank strategy_id = savings + `:all` composites (handled outside this cost join).
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    cat("  Lines with no strategy_id (savings / :all composites, expected):\n")
    print(unmatched)
  }
} else {
  cat("[SKIP S4 rekey] needs cba (S4) + REKEY_FILE.\n")
}
```

# S5. Eora26 -> GLORIA (120 products)

Each Eora26 sector maps to one or more of the 120 GLORIA products. Following the
established convention, a sector's weight is **split evenly** across its GLORIA
products (no basis to favour one). Multi-sector products then sum. Result: a
120-product weight vector per strategy, still summing to 1.

```{r eora-to-gloria}
if (have(CROSSWALK_FILE) && have(PRODUCT_NUM_FILE) && !is.null(cost_struct)) {

  # Crosswalk sheet "Eora26 - GLORIA": rows = GLORIA products, cols = Eora26 sectors,
  # cell = 1 if linked. Pivot to long (Product, Sector) pairs.
  cw <- read_excel(CROSSWALK_FILE, sheet = "Eora26 - GLORIA")
  product_col <- names(cw)[1]
  cw_long <- cw %>%
    pivot_longer(-all_of(product_col), names_to = "Sector", values_to = "linked") %>%
    filter(linked == 1) %>%
    select(-linked) %>%
    rename(Product = all_of(product_col))

  # products per sector -> even split denominator
  ppc <- cw_long %>% count(Sector, name = "n_products")

  # GLORIA product code lookup (Lfd_Nr = the code MINDSET expects)
  prod_num <- read.xlsx(PRODUCT_NUM_FILE)   # cols: Lfd_Nr, Sector_names

  # NAME-DRIFT FIX: 3 product names in the crosswalk sheet differ from the
  # product-number file (verified 1:1 bijection -> pure naming drift, same
  # product). Without this, the name join below yields product_code=NA and the
  # product's demand silently vanishes from the 120-vector. Rename crosswalk
  # side -> product-number spelling before joining.
  gloria_name_fix <- c(
    "Glass and other ceramics n.e.c."                              = "Other ceramics n.e.c.",
    "Raising of sheep and goats"                                   = "Raising of sheep",
    "Repair and installation of machinery and equipment (service)" = "Repair and installation of machinery and equipment"
  )
  cw_long <- cw_long %>%
    mutate(Product = ifelse(Product %in% names(gloria_name_fix),
                            gloria_name_fix[Product], Product))

  # DATA CHECK: which Eora26 sectors carry weight but have NO GLORIA product?
  # Their weight would silently disappear in the join. Known cases in the OLD
  # master: "Wholesale Trade", "Retail Trade", "Re-export & Re-import" (trade
  # margins the crosswalk sheet does not map). Surface them so the leakage is a
  # documented choice, not a hidden bug. If any transformation puts real weight
  # on these, add crosswalk rows or reassign before trusting its jobs number.
  unmatched <- setdiff(unique(cost_struct$Sector), unique(cw_long$Sector))
  if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
    cat("[WARN S5] Eora26 sectors with no GLORIA product (weight will drop):\n")
    print(unmatched)
    leaked <- cost_struct %>% filter(Sector %in% unmatched, weight > 0) %>%
      group_by(strategy_id) %>% summarise(lost = sum(weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(lost > 1e-6)
    if (nrow(leaked) > 0) {
      cat("  Strategies losing weight to unmapped sectors:\n"); print(as.data.frame(leaked))
    } else {
      cat("  (No strategy puts weight on an unmapped sector -> no weight actually lost.)\n")
    }
  }

  # cost_struct is keyed by (strategy_id, time_period, Sector). Carry time_period
  # through so the GLORIA vectors stay per-year (electricity mix decarbonises).
  gloria_vectors <- cost_struct %>%
    # many-to-many is EXPECTED: one Eora26 sector -> several GLORIA products.
    left_join(cw_long, by = "Sector", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    left_join(ppc,     by = "Sector") %>%
    mutate(value_product = ifelse(is.na(n_products), 0, weight / n_products)) %>%
    group_by(strategy_id, time_period, Product) %>%
    summarise(value_product = sum(value_product), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Product)) %>%
    left_join(prod_num, by = c("Product" = "Sector_names")) %>%
    rename(product_code = Lfd_Nr)

  # ASSERT the name join lost nothing: any Product with NA product_code would
  # drop that product's demand silently. Print offenders and stop if any remain.
  na_code <- gloria_vectors %>% filter(is.na(product_code)) %>% distinct(Product)
  if (nrow(na_code) > 0) {
    cat("[ERROR S5] GLORIA products with no product_code (demand would drop):\n")
    print(na_code$Product)
    stop("S5: unmatched GLORIA product name(s) -> extend gloria_name_fix above.")
  }

  # Validation: each (strategy, year) GLORIA vector sums to ~1 (below 1 = weight
  # lost to unmapped sectors; 0 = strategy has no cost structure).
  chk <- gloria_vectors %>% group_by(strategy_id, time_period) %>%
    summarise(s = sum(value_product), .groups = "drop")
  cat(sprintf("GLORIA vectors: %d strategies x %d periods; weight-sum range [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              n_distinct(gloria_vectors$strategy_id), n_distinct(gloria_vectors$time_period),
              min(chk$s), max(chk$s)))
} else {
  gloria_vectors <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S5] needs crosswalk + product numbers + cost_struct (S2).\n")
}
```

# S6. Employment: jobs = L %*% f  (domestic only)

**The payoff step.** `L` is the 120x120 matrix built by `EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py`:
`L[i, p]` = domestic jobs in product `i` per $1 of final demand booked to
product `p`. It already contains the Leontief inverse, employment coefficients,
and the import-origin split, and returns DOMESTIC jobs only. So once we have a
signed 120-product dollar vector `f` for a transformation, jobs are one
matrix product — MINDSET never runs again.

```{r load-L}
if (have(L_MATRIX_FILE)) {
  # row.names = output product code; columns = final-demand product code.
  L <- as.matrix(read.csv(L_MATRIX_FILE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
  cat(sprintf("L loaded: %d x %d. Domestic jobs per $1 (col-sum) range [%.4g, %.4g]\n",
              nrow(L), ncol(L), min(colSums(L)), max(colSums(L))))
} else {
  L <- NULL
  cat("[SKIP S6] L matrix not found. Run EXTRACT_L_MATRIX.py first.\n")
}
```

```{r jobs, eval = FALSE}
# ACTIVATES once S4 `delta` is filled and S5 vectors exist.
# Build f (length 120, ordered by product_code) per strategy and per flow, then:
#
#   dollars_by_product = value_product * cba_dollars   (per strategy, per flow)
#   f = tapply(dollars_by_product, product_code, sum)  # collapse to 120-vector
#   f = f[ as.character(1:120) ]; f[is.na(f)] <- 0
#   jobs_vec = L %*% f                                 # 120 domestic-job entries
#
# Report per strategy: gross_cost = sum(L %*% f_cost),
#                       gross_savings = sum(L %*% f_savings)  (<= 0),
#                       net = gross_cost + gross_savings.
# Keep the three side by side (job displacement is a FINDING, not to be hidden).
cat("[S6 jobs] inert until S4 delta + S5 vectors are live.\n")
```

Two products, both optional until upstream is live:

     against MINDSET's BATCH script, in the existing `Strategy_<id>_<ISO>.xlsx`
     "Investment by" format).
  2. The employment table (gross+/gross-/net by product and by strategy).
